idea: Dinner decision-and-execution system for a busy parent: onboarding -> taste calibration -> ranked 3-dinner plan -> one-tap reasoned swaps -> consolidated traceable grocery list -> prep plan -> interruption-aware cooking mode -> one-tap feedback. Mobile-first web client over a deterministic TypeScript domain package and node:sqlite, zero runtime dependencies.
spec_digest: Dinner decision-and-execution system for an interrupted parent: onboarding -> 3-meal plan -> reasoned swap -> traceable grocery list -> interruption-aware cooking -> feedback.
Deterministic core is the product: quantities, units, aggregation, inventory subtraction, dietary filtering and ranking are pure tested code - never an LLM.
The differentiator nothing else ships: per-step active/unattended/continuous-attention time, safe stopping points, validated recovery, and cooking state that survives a kill.
Non-goals: no import, no grocery integration, no notifications, no nutrition, no social, no native build, no LLM in the authoritative path.
Taste: one hand, one dominant action per screen, <=3 choices, concrete countable copy, guilt-free language, honest uncertainty, zero engagement mechanics.

decisions.decision: Mobile-first web client instead of the brief's React Native + Expo.
decisions.why: Headless Linux build machine has no iOS simulator; an Expo client could not be run, interacted with or verified and would ship unproven. Domain package is client-agnostic so an RN port consumes it unchanged later.

decisions.decision: Catalog 55 -> 30 recipes; confirmed-only inventory (defer inference layer); greedy set-scoring instead of combinatorial plan search.
decisions.why: Independent taste judge scored scope-fits-night 3/10 and named the clock, not the idea, as the failure mode. Cuts protect the interruption-aware cooking loop and the traceable grocery list - the two things prior-art scouting confirmed nobody else ships. User endorsed all three.

decisions.decision: node:sqlite built-in, zero runtime dependencies; schema stays Postgres-shaped (UUIDs, UTC, integer cents, exact numeric quantities).
decisions.why: No PostgreSQL on this host and no sudo assumed. Verified node:sqlite works on Node 24.19 at kickoff. Postgres-shaped schema keeps the later migration mechanical.

decisions.decision: Build, not adopt or extend. Treat Mealie's aggregation design as the reference bar to clear.
decisions.why: Scout grep-verified that Mealie (AGPL-3.0, gate-fail for adoption) already ships deterministic conversion + fuzzy normalization + cross-recipe aggregation with traceability, and Grocy (MIT) ships conversion chains + pantry subtraction. That engine is table stakes, not the moat. Step-level interruption metadata, package-size selection and leftover optimization are unoccupied across all five products checked.

decisions.decision: ADOPT design-panel candidate B, 'Three Good Dinners' (AMBITIOUS brief), with six ideas grafted from the losers. Locked to .swarm/DESIGN.md, which is BINDING on every builder. Architecture: three strict layers (domain/ pure + server/ node:http+node:sqlite + web/ framework-free) run directly by Node 24 native type stripping, tsc --noEmit as the strict gate and never a build step. Six invariants are non-negotiable: (1) Rational bigint num/den is the only arithmetic type on authoritative paths, qty.ts the sole entry point; (2) timers stored as absolute UTC end instants, never remaining-seconds, so DoD 7 recovery is arithmetic; (3) every db.ts helper takes household_id as a required first argument and appends the WHERE itself, making an unscoped query inexpressible; (4) swap re-ranks against the frozen remaining two meals and never re-runs planset; (5) the catalog validation gate plus the ingredient-id/allergen-class cross-check land BEFORE the recipes, not in the proof wave; (6) recovery/panic guidance reads required per-step metadata only, never fabricated. Grafted steals: single copy module with numeric slots + one shared total-vs-active time renderer (makes DoD 6 a property of one helper); user grocery edits in a separate never-overwritten column; DESIGN.md as binding contract + tokens-only CSS rule; wave-0 node:sqlite smoke check on a real file DB; receipt/ledger grocery treatment; broadened e2e.loop asserting DoD 2 and DoD 6; ephemeral-port and db-path flags on the server entrypoint as test affordances against kill-test flake.
decisions.why: Blind judge scored B 45/50 vs C 42 and A 40 across must_haves/buildability/value/coherence/depth. B was the only candidate whose calibration module deliberately SELECTS attribute-spread cards (the spec demands deliberate variance, not just reactions), and the only one to catch that DoD 9 can fail via data rather than code - an allergen present but the dietary tag unverified - forcing the cross-check early. Its delighters are additive leaves on data the spec already forces it to persist, sequenced strictly after DoD is green and individually droppable, so they cannot compromise the core. C won coherence 10 for making aesthetics enforceable as code, which is exactly right for a headless build nobody can look at - hence four of the six steals come from C. Conductor gate re-derived all three judge totals from their axes, confirmed the declared winner is the argmax, probed the winning file plan for all 17 must-have surfaces, and checked the non-goal guards (zero runtime deps, no LLM on the authoritative path): 32/32 checks passed.

decisions.decision: The CONDUCTOR authors and commits the manifests (package.json, tsconfig.json, .gitignore) and runs the installs; builders never touch them. npm test = `tsc --noEmit` then `node --test 'tests/**/*.test.ts'`. Builder worktrees are provisioned at <target>/.wt/<item-id>, NOT under /tmp, and each builder runs `npm ci` there.
decisions.why: T-001's plan notes made it 'the manifest owner (sole exception)', but build-wave.js's builder brief hard-forbids touching manifests and instructs blocking instead - the item as planned was unbuildable, and the builder would have returned blocked. cycle.md step 4 already assigns manifests to the conductor, so the conductor writing them is in-contract, not a workaround. Separately: agent file-edit tools are confined to the session's allowed directories, so build-wave.js Step 0's /tmp worktree is git-writable but NOT edit-writable - every builder would stall part-way. Both mechanisms (in-repo worktree + npm ci, and the full tsc/node --test/node:sqlite pipeline) were proven BY THE CONDUCTOR on this host before any agent was dispatched; the wave then ran first-try clean.

decisions.decision: RecipeStep's nine required interruption fields use two names that differ from SPEC.md: `maximum_pause` (union {kind:'bounded',seconds} | {kind:'unlimited'}) instead of `maximum_pause_seconds`, and `timer_duration_seconds` (number | null) instead of `timer_duration`. `recovery_instruction` is likewise a union ({kind:'instruction',text} | {kind:'none_available'}) rather than a bare string. ACCEPTED as-is; the notes of T-008, T-009, T-010 and T-011 now carry the real names.
decisions.why: The must-have's substance is that all nine fields exist and are REQUIRED on every step - verified, all nine are non-optional readonly members. The identifiers are internal. Both renames are improvements: an explicit unit suffix, and explicit unions instead of null/sentinel magic, which is exactly what Invariant 6 ('no guidance available must be representable, not absent') asks for. Recorded rather than silently normalised because recipe JSON authored against the SPEC names would fail the catalog gate at 5am - the precise 'DoD 9 fails via data' failure the design panel predicted.

decisions.decision: Cycle 4 died between its merges and its verification gate: both builder branches were merged to master (860d034, ade40ef) but state.json, backlog.json, the journal and the runfile were never written, and no gate ran. Cycle 5 completed cycle 4 rather than starting new work — authored the gates from scratch, ran them, and closed the wave.
decisions.why: Merged-but-ungated code is the single most dangerous state this pipeline can be in: master carries work that LOOKS verified because it is committed, and hard rule 4 (green main) had never actually been checked. Dispatching a new wave on top would have compounded unverified work. The salvage rule in cycle.md step 2 covers dirty trees; this was the rarer case of a CLEAN tree whose bookkeeping was a cycle behind — detectable only because the commit messages said cycle 4 while state.json said cycle 3.

decisions.decision: T-002's domain/src/ingredients.ts is CUT from scope. catalog.ts (landed by T-008) already owns the curated ingredient registry — aliases, allergen classes, densities, per-item weights — sourced from data/ingredients.json. normalize.ts consumes IngredientRegistry as a parameter instead of owning a second table.
decisions.why: A second curated table would be a second source of truth, which is precisely the data-drift failure Invariant 5 exists to prevent. Ruled at cycle 6 dispatch time and recorded in the in-flight marker; formalised here because the cycle that made the ruling died before it could write a journal block.

decisions.decision: Cycle 6 was killed mid-wave by the pacer's 600s background-task ceiling ("Background tasks still running after 600s; terminating", runs/pacer.log 22:55Z). This session RESUMED cycle 6 rather than opening cycle 7: merged wave-006-T-002 (complete and committed by its builder), salvage-committed the T-006 builder's uncommitted worktree files, merged those too, then authored and ran both verification gates.
decisions.why: The in-flight marker cycle 6 wrote at dispatch (D-8's lesson from cycle 4) worked exactly as designed — it named the branches, the worktrees and the recovery procedure, so this session lost no time diagnosing. The T-006 builder had written filters.ts, score.ts and filters.test.ts but not score.test.ts; that work was coherent and self-contained (imports only frozen modules), so salvaging beat discarding 1,370 lines and rebuilding. What the salvage CANNOT do is invent the missing regression tests — filed as T-029 rather than papered over.

decisions.decision: Cycle 7 dispatched its two builders as DIRECT, FOREGROUND Agent calls editing the main working tree under strictly disjoint file scopes — no build-wave workflow, no worktrees, no builder branches. Both builders were forbidden to run any git command; the conductor committed.
decisions.why: KI-4 killed cycles 4 and 6 mid-wave. This cycle established the mechanism: bin/swarm-pacer.sh spawns `claude -p` synchronously with NO timeout of its own (verified by reading lines 232-260), so the 600s guillotine is purely the harness background-task wait ceiling (CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS, default 600000) applied at turn end. Foreground agents are part of the turn, not background tasks, so the ceiling never applies. The wave ran 424s and 356s — both would have been at risk, and the T-029 builder in particular was still working at the 356s mark. This is a prompt-side workaround costing nothing; the durable fix is still in the pacer and still belongs in the morning report.

decisions.decision: A backlog item whose deliverable is a TEST FILE is gated by MUTATION TESTING, not by a green suite. T-029 was verified by injecting 13 deliberate defects into score.ts one at a time and requiring the committed suite to go red for each.
decisions.why: A file of assert.ok(true) passes npm test. For T-029 specifically the whole point was that score.ts had zero committed coverage, so accepting `suite green` as evidence would have re-created the exact hole the item existed to close. The method paid for itself immediately: 11 of 13 mutants died, but two survived and revealed a precise, non-obvious gap (penalties are read back from the engine rather than pinned as literals, so penalty-amount drift mutates test and engine in lockstep). That gap is invisible to every other form of review.

known_issues.desc: Kickoff step-5 settings.json edit DENIED by the harness (recurrence of the SWARM-side KI-2 seen on the moon run for 24 consecutive runs). Two consequences: (a) permissions.additionalDirectories stays [], so every headless cycle depends on swarm-pacer.sh passing --add-dir /opt/targets/dinner explicitly - a relaunch that omits it will stall on permission prompts; (b) bin/swarm-budget.sh and bin/swarm-playbook.sh remain unallowlisted, so the budget probe and playbook parser cannot run from a headless conductor and must be worked around (budget seeded from the last real probe; playbook apply_mode read by direct file read). SWARM-side tooling gap, not a target defect. Hard rule 5 forbids fixing it from inside a run - it belongs in the morning report.

RE-OPENED at cycle 5 (was mislabelled RESOLVED-BY-DRIFT at cycle 3). The weekly governor zero-envelope blind spot in bin/swarm-weekly-from-allocator.sh: heat is computed as 100*swarm_used/(swarm_used+allow_overall), so a zero denominator DISENGAGES the governor. At cycle 3 swarm_used_pct had drifted 0 -> 4 and I recorded the bug as resolved. At cycle 5 it fell back to 0 with allow_overall_pct 0 and posture "trickle", so the feeder would disengage the governor again — precisely when restraint matters most. The ceiling held at 2 this cycle ONLY because a second, independent signal was hot (raw account 52.0% weekly at 24.65% week-elapsed => heat 2.11). Drift is not a fix. Correct behaviour: u+a <= 0 must mean MAXIMUM heat, not "unconfigured". Hard rule 5 forbids the fix mid-run; morning report.

SWARM-side, workflows/build-wave.js. Its builder Step 0 hardcodes a /tmp worktree (mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/wave-<id>.XXXXXX"). On this host, agent file-edit tools are confined to the session's allowed directories (/opt/swarm, /opt/targets/<target>), so a /tmp worktree is writable by git but NOT by the builder's own Write/Edit tools: every builder would provision successfully, then stall or fail part-way through its first edit. Worked around this cycle by a conductor `context` override pointing the worktree at <target>/.wt/<item-id> (gitignored) plus an `npm ci` there; the wave then ran clean first try. The durable fix is to derive the worktree root from projectDir in build-wave.js rather than TMPDIR. Second, smaller gap in the same file: it passes the backlog's effort value straight to agent({effort}), but the backlog uses S/M/L while the harness expects low/medium/high - the conductor mapped L->high at dispatch. Hard rule 5 forbids editing the script mid-run; both belong in the morning report.

SWARM-side. The headless pacer kills a cycle's background tasks after 600s ("Background tasks still running after 600s; terminating" — runs/pacer.log 2026-08-18T22:55Z), but build-wave's own duration budget is 2700s. Any wave whose builders run past 10 minutes is guillotined mid-flight: cycle 6 lost its workflow return, its journal block and one builder's test file this way, and cycle 4 died the same way earlier in the run. The conductor's in-flight marker makes this RECOVERABLE (cycle 6 was resumed and closed cleanly), but every occurrence costs a cycle and can leave merged-but-ungated code. Fix direction: set CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS to match the wave budget in bin/swarm-pacer.sh, or have the pacer read the wave-duration table. Hard rule 5 forbids the fix mid-run; morning report.
